subject: OrionAI: Dedicated capacity schedule conflict and prioritization
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@orionai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <pri.desai@orionai.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrionAI Q3 committed ramp — conflict on reserved lanes

Rafael / Monica,

Quick heads up — we just got notified that our Q3 model rollout (internal product M1 -> M2) will need reserved inference capacity starting 2027-07-01, with an initial ramp that will need sustained throughput equivalent to ~8 x A100-ish GPUs during peak hours. Our procurement timeline is tight; procurement needs a firm plan (SOW + resource lock) by next week so we can finalize budgets.

We understand there are several existing reserved deals in the same tranche window. Can we get clarity on whether our reservation can be honored, and if not, what prioritization logic Redwood will apply? We are willing to consider a mix of burst + baseline reservations if that helps.

Also appreciate any visibility into fallback model variants (quantized) you can suggest so we can scope quality trade-offs.

Attaching our internal ramp spreadsheet for context.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Carter
Head of Infrastructure Engineering, OrionAI
Attachments: orion_ramp_plan.xlsx (sent separately)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@orionai.com>, Priya Desai <pri.desai@orionai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrionAI Q3 committed ramp — conflict on reserved lanes

Sam / Priya — thanks for the heads up and the spreadsheet. We pulled this into the capacity workstream and I wanted to propose a short, explicit decision framework so procurement has something concrete to review:

1) Capacity lattice: prioritize committed reserved deals by (a) signed SOW effective date, (b) committed GPU-hours per month, (c) revenue impact/penalty clauses. If there is a tie we use a fairness-weighted split for the first 30 days and then re-evaluate.

2) Soft-reserve + burst: for near-term conflicts we can offer a baseline soft-reserve (guaranteed baseline throughput) plus a burst pool for peak hours. Burst will be subject to preemption rules that are explicit in the SOW.

3) Degradation ladder: recommend OrionAI prepare a fallback profile (quantized 8-bit or smaller model variant + batching) and a degraded SLA for burst-preempt windows; we can document expected latency/cost deltas.

I'm attaching a capacity_lattice_workbook.xlsx with two proposed lane assignments and preemption windows. Marissa / Vivek / Karthik — please review and flag any infra/ops constraints by EOD tomorrow so we can share an SOW draft with Orion.

Action: Rafael to sync legal on SOW language for preemption and credits; Monica to draft SOW annex for lane assignment.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachments: capacity_lattice_workbook.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Carter <sam.carter@orionai.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: capacity lattice proposal — infra mapping and fallback options

Looping infra details into the thread. Quick notes from ops:

- Feasibility: the two lane assignment options in the workbook map to existing p5d / p4d pools. Option A (strict reserved) consumes 8 GPUs in tranche-3 region us-west-2 across 00:00-10:00 UTC daily — this will push other low-priority burst customers into a shared burst pool. Option B (baseline+burst) keeps 4 GPUs hard-reserved and adds a 4-GPU burst buffer.

- Preemption mechanics: burst buffer preemption will favor (1) SLAs with hard-reserve, (2) customers with higher penalty clauses, then (3) chronological commit order. Preemption notifications will be emitted via webhook + email 5 minutes prior to soft-eviction.

- Fallbacks: for quantized model variants we recommend the following presets for OrionAI to evaluate: q8_compat (minimal perf hit), q4_aggressive (larger perf drop, much lower cost). We can run a quick evaluation (2–3 days) on their sample prompt set.

Risk: if we accept Option A without rebalancing other tranches, we expect a ~12% spike in queue latency for best-effort customers during first 2 weeks of ramp. That's manageable but needs comms.

I'll join the SOW review if Rafael schedules it.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Planning
From: Priya Desai <pri.desai@orionai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Carter <sam.carter@orionai.com>, Cloud Sales <cloudsales@stratuscloud.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrionAI Q3 committed ramp — acceptance of baseline+burst proposal

Rafael / team,

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the workbook — we reviewed Option B (baseline+burst) and that aligns with our internal risk profile. We accept a 4-GPU hard-reserve + 4-GPU shared burst buffer with the following conditions:

- Preemption notice must be at least 5 minutes and include estimated backfill window.
- During preemption windows we will accept a degraded SLA but require a 10% service credit for sustained >3 minute evictions per day.
- Redwood to run q8_compat profiling on our sample prompts and share latency/cost delta before we sign final SOW.

Procurement is looping in contracting; please send the SOW + annex and the DocuSign link. We can sign within 48 hours if the SOW matches the workbook.

Priya
Priya Desai
VP Product Operations, OrionAI

Subject: Re: OrionAI: Dedicated capacity schedule conflict and prioritization — decision & next steps

Team — summary and action items:

Decision: accept OrionAI on Option B (4-GPU hard-reserve + 4-GPU shared burst) effective 2027-07-01 with the preemption windows and service-credit language Priya requested (legal to confirm exact wording).

Action items:
- Monica: draft SOW + annex with lane assignment and preemption procedure; include webhook notification spec and 5-minute notice SLA. Due: Mon 2027-04-19 EOD.
- Marissa: update capacity ledger and adjust tranche-3 scheduling to accommodate the burst buffer. Notify impacted best-effort customers with a short comms note. Due: Tue 2027-04-20.
- Vivek/Karthik: run q8_compat profiling on Orion sample prompts (2–3 business days) and share a one-pager with latency/cost deltas. Due: Wed 2027-04-21.
- Rafael: coordinate with Legal and Sales Ops to finalize DocuSign link once SOW is ready.

I'll schedule a 30-min alignment call for Monday to walk the SOW annex and comms plan. Sam/Priya — thanks for being flexible. We'll aim to keep disruption to other customers minimal and document the lattice so future conflicts can be resolved faster.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
